title: Configure clients to connect via mcp-front
description: Set up Claude Code, Claude.ai, and Cursor on other devices to connect to mcp-front on the NAS over Tailscale. Document the connection config for each client type.

title: Deploy and test mcp-front on NAS
description: Install/run mcp-front on the NAS with the config. Verify it starts, health check passes, and SSE endpoints respond. Test connecting from another device on the tailnet.

title: Expose NAS MCP servers to all devices via mcp-front over Tailscale
description:
## Goal

Access MCP servers running as Docker containers on the NAS from any device on the tailnet — Claude Code, Claude.ai, and Cursor.

## Architecture

- NAS: Custom Linux box on Tailscale, running MCP servers as Docker containers
- mcp-front: Auth proxy that sits in front of MCP servers, exposing them over HTTP (SSE)
- Clients connect to http://<nas-tailscale-ip>:8080/<service>/sse

## Key Questions to Investigate

1. What MCP containers are currently running on the NAS?
2. Can the NAS run mcp-front (Go binary or Docker)?
3. What auth approach to use? (bearer tokens simplest for Tailscale private network)
4. What config is needed to map mcp-front to existing MCP containers?
5. How do clients (Claude Code, Claude.ai, Cursor) each connect?

title: Create mcp-front config for NAS MCP servers
description: Based on the audit of running containers, write a config.json with bearer token auth (simplest for Tailscale private network). Map each MCP server to an endpoint. Set baseURL to the NAS Tailscale IP.

title: Check NAS environment for running mcp-front
description: Verify what's available on the NAS to run mcp-front: Go installed? Docker available? Architecture (amd64/arm64)? This determines whether to run mcp-front as a native binary or Docker container.

title: Audit running MCP containers on NAS
description: SSH into the NAS and run docker ps to catalog what MCP servers are currently running. Document container names, images, ports, and any volume mounts. This determines what mcp-front needs to proxy to.
